detaileddescription.para: Use the anonymous constructor, and pass the name to add_top_suite(), which can also override the name given here.

parameterdescription.para: The name given to the top suite.

detaileddescription.para: The constructor initialises a new runner instance together with its top suite (top_suite_). If tracing is enabled, it outputs the function signature for diagnostic purposes.

detaileddescription.para: Equivalent to initialise (argc, argv) followed by add_top_suite (top_suite_name). Use the two calls; the top suite is now optional, and initialise() no longer returns it.
The name no longer has a default value, so that the call with two arguments selects the current initialise (argc, argv), which returns nothing and does not add the top suite.
If the runner is already initialised, or the test execution was aborted, the error is reported on stderr, as by initialise(), and the top suite is returned without other effects.

parameterdescription.para: The name given to the top suite; if empty, the name is chosen as by add_top_suite().

If the runner is already initialised, or the test execution was aborted, the error is reported by initialise(), and the top suite is returned without being added.

detaileddescription.para: Calls run_suites(); once the session has ended, it only returns the exit code.
Kept for compatibility; it calls run_suites(), so the first call runs the session and the later ones return the stored exit code.

detaileddescription.para: Calls add_suite(). The old name did not show that the suite is only stored, to be run later by run_suites(), unlike the test cases, which run immediately; it also hid the suite class inside the runner.

The types of the callable arguments.
The test suite name or description, as for add_suite().

Forwards to verbosity_level().

detaileddescription.para: In v5.0.1, the runner was a test node, and always returned "runner". The runner is no longer a node; the name shown at the beginning of the reports is that of the top suite, returned by add_top_suite().
Returns the constant string "runner", as before the runner stopped being a test node.

briefdescription.para: Deprecated count of the test suites added with add_suite(), plus the top suite.

detaileddescription.para: Returns added_suites_count() plus one, for the top suite. The name suggested that all the suites are counted, while the static suites are not. Use added_suites_count(), plus one for the top suite, or total_suites_count().

simplesect.para: The number of test suites added with add_suite(), plus one.

briefdescription.para: Deprecated access to the timings of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the internal stopwatch of the session, started by initialise() and stopped at the end of run_suites(); the elapsed time is complete only after run_suites() has returned. In v5.0.1, the returned class was detail::timestamps, now a deprecated alias; only its read-only members are kept. The timings are internal; the elapsed times are shown by the reporters.

detaileddescription.para: Kept for the v5.0.1 code that binds a non-const reference (detail::timestamps& t = tr.timings ();). The test code must not start or stop the stopwatch through it, since the reporters show its elapsed time.

simplesect.para: A reference to the stopwatch of the session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a reference to the stopwatch member.

briefdescription.para: Deprecated access to the reporter of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the internal reporter, created by initialise(), as selected by the session options; the call is valid only after initialise(). In v5.0.1, the returned class was the top namespace reporter, now detail::reporter; of its members, the applications used only verbosity(), kept, deprecated, on detail::reporter.

simplesect.para: A reference to the reporter of the session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a reference to the reporter owned by the reporter_ unique pointer, which is empty before initialise().
Constructed; initialise() not yet called.
Initialised; test cases may be added and run.
run_suites() runs the suites; no suite may be added.
All suites run and the session ended.

briefdescription.para: The states of a test session.

detaileddescription.para: The session moves only forwards, from created to initialised (by initialise()), to running, and to finished (both by run_suites()); the calls made in another state are reported or ignored.

briefdescription.para: The type of the function called when test execution is aborted.

detaileddescription.para: The handler receives the source location from which the abort was triggered. It is not expected to return; it may, for example, reset an embedded target, or signal the test result to a debugger. If it returns, the process is terminated with ::abort().

When exceptions are enabled, it may also throw an exception, to return control to the application without terminating the process. The test cases and the suites do not catch it, so it leaves the test() call that started a test case of the top suite, or run_suites(), and reaches the application; their remaining code is not run. The report is complete, but the runner cannot be used afterwards (see abort()).

briefdescription.para: The human reporter, which displays the session.

detaileddescription.para: It reads the stopwatch, to display the duration of the session.

briefdescription.para: The TAP reporter, which displays the session.

detaileddescription.para: It reads the stopwatch, to display the duration of the session.

briefdescription.para: The base of the nodes, which shares the state of the session.

detaileddescription.para: It passes the reporter to the suites and the test cases, applies the filter, lists the test cases, keeps the running test case, and aborts for a failed requirement.

briefdescription.para: The static suites link themselves through the runner.

detaileddescription.para: The static_suite constructors call link_static_suite(), which rejects the suites constructed after run_suites() has started.

briefdescription.para: The head of the list of the runners that have started.

detaileddescription.para: Constant-initialised, so it is valid before any constructor runs. A runner is inserted by run_suites() and removed by the destructor.
Constant-initialised, so it is null before any static constructor runs.

briefdescription.para: The function called by abort(), if not null.

detaileddescription.para: Set by set_abort_handler().

briefdescription.para: Whether the test execution was aborted.

detaileddescription.para: Set by abort(), before the abort is reported, and never cleared. Read by detail::runnable_base, a friend, so that, when the abort handler throws an exception, the test cases and the suites pass it on instead of reporting it, and no test case runs afterwards; read by initialise() and run_suites(), which then refuse to start, and by abort(), so that a later abort is not reported again.

briefdescription.para: Owning collection of dynamically registered child suites.

detaileddescription.para: Each call to add_suite() appends a new suite to this vector, and inserts it into the list of suites, sorted by name; the suites are run later, by run_suites(), in the order of the list. The vector retains ownership of all suites for the lifetime of the runner.

briefdescription.para: The exit code computed by run_suites().

detaileddescription.para: Returned again by the calls of run_suites() made after the session ended.

briefdescription.para: Whether a suite was added after run_suites() had started.

detaileddescription.para: Set by register_suite(), which rejects such a suite; run_suites() then returns 1, unless an option error requires 2.

briefdescription.para: Whether the top suite was added to the session.

detaileddescription.para: Set by add_top_suite(). When not set, the top suite is neither run, nor reported, nor counted.

briefdescription.para: The suite whose name was listed last, if any.

detaileddescription.para: Used by list_test_case() to write the name of a suite only once, before its first listed test case.

briefdescription.para: The number of suites with listed test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Incremented by list_test_case() when it writes the name of a suite; written by run_suites() at the end of the list.

briefdescription.para: The number of listed test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Incremented by list_test_case(); written by run_suites() at the end of the list.

briefdescription.para: The options of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: Moved in by initialise(), and kept for the whole session: the verbosity is returned by verbosity_level(), the filter patterns are read by is_selected(), the listing of the test cases by run_suites() and is_listing(), and the command line by the reporters, which are friends. The defaults until then.

briefdescription.para: Owning pointer to the test reporter used for outputting test results.

detaileddescription.para: Created by initialise(), as selected by the session options, either given by the caller or parsed from the command line by the runner_options constructor. Used by the suites and the test cases, through detail::runnable_base, which is a friend.

briefdescription.para: The innermost test case being run, if any.

detaileddescription.para: Set by detail::runnable_base, a friend, while a test case runs, and restored when it ends, so that suite::test(), when called from the body of a test case (for example via a captured suite reference), runs the new test case nested in it.

briefdescription.para: The current state of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: Set by initialise() and run_suites(); read by register_suite(), to reject the suites added too late.

briefdescription.para: The number of suites skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Incremented by run_child_suites(); returned by skipped_suites_count().

briefdescription.para: The next runner in the list of the started runners.

detaileddescription.para: Null if this runner has not started, or is the last one.

briefdescription.para: Stopwatch of this runner.

detaileddescription.para: Measures the duration of the entire test session; started by initialise(), stopped by run_suites(), and read by the reporters, which are friends.

briefdescription.para: The top suite, whose body is the code of main().

detaileddescription.para: Always constructed with the runner, but part of the session only after add_top_suite() (see has_top_suite_); its test cases are added directly, between add_top_suite() and run_suites().

briefdescription.para: Owned storage for the top suite name.

detaileddescription.para: Set by add_top_suite(), either from its argument or derived from arguments[0] of the session options.

briefdescription.para: Totals of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: The totals of each suite are added by run_suites() and run_child_suites(), after the suite was run.

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy constructor to prevent copying.

detaileddescription.para: The runner owns the suites, the reporter, and the session totals, which must not be duplicated.

briefdescription.para: Deleted move constructor to prevent moving.

detaileddescription.para: The suites keep a reference to the runner, so it must not be relocated.

briefdescription.para: Constructor for the runner class.

detaileddescription.para: The session is configured later, by initialise(), and the top suite, if any, is added by add_top_suite().

Parameters
None.
The constructor initialises a new runner instance together with its top suite (top_suite_). If tracing is enabled, it outputs the function signature for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Destructor for the runner class.

detaileddescription.para: Destroys the registered suites and the reporter, which closes the output file, if any. The static suites are not owned by the runner.
The reporter_ unique pointer is released automatically. If tracing is enabled, the function signature is output for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Aborts test execution immediately.

detaileddescription.para: Between initialise() and the end of run_suites(), the reporter completes the report, on the console and in the output file: it writes the results of the running test case, if any, followed by a line with the source location (a Bail out! line with the TAP reporter), in place of the totals. Before initialise() or after run_suites(), when there is no report to complete, the source location is written to stderr.
The handler set by set_abort_handler() is then called, if any. If there is no handler, or if it returns, the process is terminated with ::abort().

The abort is final, also when the handler throws an exception: no test case runs afterwards, initialise() and run_suites() report an error on stderr (run_suites() returns 1), and a later abort is not reported again.

sl
The source location from which the abort is triggered.
Returns
Does not return.
Delegates to abort(), as an explicit abort, not caused by a failed requirement.

briefdescription.para: Adds a test suite to the runner, to be run by run_suites().

detaileddescription.para: Unlike the test cases added to the top suite (see add_top_suite()), which run immediately, the suite is only stored; run_suites() runs it later, together with the static suites that refer to this runner, sorted by name.

The suites must be added before run_suites() is called. A suite added while run_suites() runs (for example from the body of another suite), or after it returned, would never run; it is rejected, the error is reported on stderr, and the exit code is not 0, so that the omission cannot pass unnoticed.

Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test suite name or description, used in reports; a string literal, a const char*, a std::string, or a std::string_view. It is copied, so the string need not outlive the call, nor be null-terminated.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test suite.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
6.0.0
Constructs a suite object on the heap, binding the callable and any additional arguments, then transfers ownership to the runner via register_suite(). The suite is not run here; all registered suites are run later by run_suites(), together with the static suites, sorted by name. A suite added once run_suites() has started is rejected by register_suite().

briefdescription.para: Adds the top suite and returns it.

detaileddescription.para: The top suite is the suite whose body is the code of main(): its test cases run immediately, when test() is called, before the suites added with add_suite() and the static suites, which run later, by run_suites(). It is always the first suite in the report.
The call is optional; without it, there is no top suite, and only the other suites are run and reported. If the runner is not yet initialised, it is initialised with the default options.
If no name is given, here or by the deprecated constructor, the top suite is named after the file name of runner_options::arguments[0], without the extension, when available, or "default suite".

The top suite can be added only once, and before run_suites(); a second call, or a call made once run_suites() has started, is reported on stderr, and the existing top suite is returned. With an unknown reporter name, the top suite is returned, but nothing is reported.

top_suite_name
The name of the top suite, used in reports; a string literal, a const char*, a std::string, or a std::string_view. It is copied, so the string need not outlive the call, nor be null-terminated. Defaults to an empty string.
Reference to the top suite.
6.0.0
Initialises the runner with the default options, if not yet done, names the top suite, marks it as part of the session, starts its timing, and emits the reporter notification for its beginning; while the test cases are listed, the top suite is not reported.

If the name is empty, the name given to the deprecated constructor is kept; if there is none, the name is derived from the file name of arguments[0] (usually argv[0]), without the extension, or defaults to "default suite".

After the test execution was aborted, the error is reported on stderr. With an unknown reporter, the session has already finished, and the top suite is returned without other effects. A second call, or a call once run_suites() has started, is reported on stderr; the latter also sets has_rejected_suites_, so that the exit code is not 0.

briefdescription.para: Returns the count of the test suites added with add_suite().

detaileddescription.para: The count includes neither the top suite nor the static suites, which are counted by static_suites_count(); add one for the top suite, if added, or use total_suites_count(), which counts all of them. The suites that add_suite() rejects, once run_suites() has started, are not counted.

Parameters
None.
The number of test suites added with add_suite().
6.0.0
Returns the number of suites stored by register_suite(); the top suite and the static suites are not in children_suites_.

briefdescription.para: Initialises the test runner with the command-line arguments.

detaileddescription.para: Parses the command-line options and initialises the runner with them; equivalent to initialise (runner_options{ argc, argv }).

The call is optional; without it, the runner is initialised with the default options by the first call of add_top_suite() or run_suites(). If used, it must therefore precede them; a later call, or a call after the test execution was aborted, reports an error on stderr, without other effects; the options are then not parsed, so their errors do not change the exit code.

argc
The argument count from main().
argv
The argument vector from main().
Returns
Nothing.
6.0.0
Parses the command-line options with the runner_options constructor, and initialises the runner with them.

The options are not parsed if the runner is already initialised, or the test execution was aborted, since an option error would change the exit code of the session; the error is reported by the overload taking the options.
If tracing is enabled, the command-line arguments are also logged for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Initialises the test runner with the given options.

detaileddescription.para: Creates the reporter selected by the options and starts the session. The options may be parsed from the command line, adjusted, and passed here:

The call is optional; without it, the runner is initialised with the default options by the first call of add_top_suite() or run_suites(). If used, it must therefore precede them; a later call, or a call after the test execution was aborted, reports an error on stderr, without other effects.

If the output file cannot be opened, the error is reported on stderr and the report is written only to the console; the tests are still run, but run_suites() returns 2. With an unknown reporter name, nothing is reported, no test is run, and run_suites() returns 2.
The options are taken by value and moved into the runner, which keeps them for the whole session; pass a temporary, or use std::move(), to avoid a copy.

options
The session options.
Returns
Nothing.
6.0.0
Moves the options into the runner, which keeps them for the whole session, creates the reporter selected by them, starts the session timing, and emits the initial reporter notification for the session. While the test cases are listed, only the header of the list is written; the session is not reported.
If the output file cannot be opened, the reporter writes only to the console, and run_suites() will return 2.
If the reporter name is not recognised, nothing else is done: no output file is created, nothing is reported, the session is marked as finished, so that no test is run, and run_suites() returns 2.
The runner is initialised only once; a later call, or a call after the test execution was aborted, reports an error on stderr, without other effects.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether the test cases are listed instead of run.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the --list-tests (or --list) command-line option, or by runner_options::list_tests. While the test cases are listed, their bodies do not run, so the code in main() or in the suite bodies that depends on their results (their totals, or the exit code of run_suites()) can use it to skip those parts, and the tests can use it to keep their own messages out of the list. Before initialise() is called, it is false.

Parameters
None.
true
The test cases are listed.
false
The test cases are run.
6.0.0
Returns runner_options::list_tests of the session options.

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy assignment operator to prevent copying.

detaileddescription.para: The runner owns the suites, the reporter, and the session totals, which must not be duplicated.

briefdescription.para: Deleted move assignment operator to prevent moving.

detaileddescription.para: The suites keep a reference to the runner, so it must not be relocated.

briefdescription.para: Runs the registered suites, ends the session, and returns the exit code.

detaileddescription.para: Completes the top suite, if any, runs the suites registered with add_suite() and the static suites that refer to this runner, together, sorted by name, and ends the session. If the runner is not yet initialised, it is initialised with the default options. When filter patterns are given, the suites whose names do not match the first pattern are reported as skipped, without being run.

While the test cases are listed (see is_listing()), the suites run only to create their test cases, which are listed, and the number of listed test cases is written; the result of the checks does not affect the exit code, since no check is evaluated.
A session without any suite (no top suite, no suite added with add_suite(), and no static suite) is reported as an error, since a test program that runs nothing must not pass unnoticed.

The session runs only once; later calls return the same exit code without running anything again. A call made while the session runs, for example from a suite body, or after the test execution was aborted (see abort()), is reported on stderr and returns 1, without other effects.

Parameters
None.
0 if all checks passed, or if the test cases were listed; 1 if a check failed, if a suite was rejected by add_suite() or add_top_suite(), if there was no suite, if the runner is running, or if the test execution was aborted; 2 if initialise() reported an option error, or if the filters selected no test case, regardless of the checks.
6.0.0
Initialises the runner with the default options, if not yet done. Finalises the top suite, if added, by stopping its stopwatch and notifying the reporter, then accumulates its totals into the runner totals. Subsequently invokes run_child_suites() to execute, sorted by name, and accumulate the registered and the static child suites. Finally, stops the session stopwatch, notifies the reporter, and returns 0 if all checks passed or 1 otherwise, or if a suite was rejected by register_suite() or add_top_suite(), or if there was no suite at all; if initialise() reported an option error, or if the filters selected no test case, 2 is returned, regardless of the checks.
While the suites run, the session is in the running state, so that the suites added by them are rejected.

While the test cases are listed, the top suite is not reported, the suites run only to create their test cases, the numbers of listed test cases and suites end the list, and the exit code is 0, or 2 after an option error.

The result is stored, and the later calls return it without running anything again. If the runner is already running (a call from a suite or a test case), or if the test execution was aborted, an error is reported on stderr and 1 is returned.

briefdescription.para: Sets the function called when test execution is aborted.

detaileddescription.para: Test execution is aborted by a failed require(), when exceptions are not enabled (otherwise only the test case is stopped), or by an explicit call of abort(). The abort is reported before the handler is called (see abort()).
The handler can be set at any time, before or after initialise().

handler
The new handler, or nullptr to restore the default behaviour, which terminates the process with ::abort().
The previous handler, or nullptr if none was set.
6.0.0
Stores the new handler and returns the previous one; a null handler restores the default behaviour.

briefdescription.para: Returns the count of the test suites skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Counts the suites, registered or static, whose names do not match the first filter pattern (--filter or runner_options::filter_patterns); it is complete only after run_suites() has returned, and is zero when there are no patterns. The skipped suites are included in added_suites_count() and static_suites_count(); the skipped test cases are counted by counters::skipped_test_cases().

Parameters
None.
The number of test suites that were not run.
6.0.0
Returns the counter incremented by run_child_suites().

briefdescription.para: Returns the count of static test suites.

detaileddescription.para: Counts the static_suite objects that refer to this runner; it is complete only after the static initialisation.

Parameters
None.
The number of static test suites run by this runner.
Walks the list of suites, counts those that refer to this runner, and subtracts the suites registered with add_suite(), which are all in the list.

briefdescription.para: Returns the count of all the test suites.

detaileddescription.para: One, if the top suite was added by add_top_suite(), plus added_suites_count() plus static_suites_count(); this is the number of suites printed by the reporters.

Parameters
None.
The total number of test suites managed by this runner, including the top suite, if any, and the static suites.
Returns one, if the top suite was added, plus the count of the suites added with add_suite(), plus the count of the static suites.

briefdescription.para: Gets the totals of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: The counters include the checks and the test cases of all the suites that were run, including the top suite, if any; they are complete only after run_suites() has returned. The totals are read-only; there is no non-const overload, so that the counters cannot be modified from the test code.

Parameters
None.
A const reference to the session totals.
Returns a const reference to the counters member.

briefdescription.para: Returns the verbosity level of the console output.

detaileddescription.para: The level is selected with the --silent, --quiet, and --verbose command-line options, or with runner_options::verbosity_level; the tests can use it to decide whether to display their own messages. Before initialise() is called, it is verbosity::normal.

Parameters
None.
The active verbosity value.
6.0.0
Returns the level kept in options_, which does not depend on the reporter, so the call is safe before initialise().

briefdescription.para: Aborts test execution, telling the reporter why.

detaileddescription.para: Implements abort(), which calls it for an explicit abort; also called by detail::runnable_base, a friend, for a failed requirement without exceptions, so that the reporter names the cause.

sl
The source location from which the abort is triggered.
is_requirement
true if the abort is caused by a failed requirement.
Returns
Does not return.
While the report is open, from initialise(), which begins it (the test cases of the top suite run from then on), to the end of run_suites(), the reporter writes the buffered results and the location of the abort, with abort_session(), to the console and to the output file, since the totals are never reached. Otherwise, there is no report to complete, and the location is written to stderr. The standard streams are then flushed, and the handler set by set_abort_handler() is called, if any. If there is no handler, or if it returns, the process is terminated via ::abort().

The aborted_ flag is set first, and never cleared, so that, if the handler throws an exception, the test cases and the suites pass it on (see test_case::run()), and the runner refuses to run again. An abort after another one, for example from the code that caught the exception, is not reported again, since the report is already complete; the handler is still called.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether an option error was found by initialise().

detaileddescription.para: Called by run_suites(), which then returns 2. The errors are those found while parsing the options (see runner_options::has_errors()), and the output file that cannot be opened. The filters that select no test case are checked by run_suites() itself.
Valid only after initialise() created the reporter.

true if an option error was found.
Combines the results kept by the options and by the reporter, so that the runner needs no flag of its own.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a suite or a test case is selected by the filter pattern of its nesting level.

detaileddescription.para: Level 0 refers to the suites, level 1 to their test cases, and each further level to the test cases nested one level deeper. A name is selected when there is no pattern for its level, or when it matches one of the alternatives of the pattern, separated by |, as defined by utility::is_match().
Also called by detail::runnable_base, a friend, before running a test case.

name
The name of the suite or of the test case.
level
The nesting level; 0 for suites.
true if it must run, false if it must be skipped.
The levels beyond the last pattern are not filtered. Otherwise, the alternatives of the pattern, separated by |, are tried in order, until one matches the whole name.

briefdescription.para: Lists a test case, instead of running it.

detaileddescription.para: Called by detail::runnable_base, a friend, for each selected test case created while the test cases are listed (see runner_options::list_tests). The name of the suite is written before its first listed test case, indented by two spaces, and the name of the test case after it, indented by four spaces, through the reporter, to the console, unless the verbosity is silent, and to the output file, if any.

suite
The suite of the test case.
test_case
The test case to list.
Returns
Nothing.
The suites are listed in the order in which their first test cases are created: the top suite first, during main(), then the other suites, in the order of run_child_suites(); so the name of a suite is written when it differs from the previous one.

briefdescription.para: Registers a test suite with the runner.

detaileddescription.para: Called by add_suite(). Once run_suites() has started, the suite is rejected: it is destroyed, the error is reported on stderr, and has_rejected_suites_ is set.

suite
Owning pointer to the test suite to register.
Returns
Nothing.
Takes ownership of the supplied suite unique pointer and appends it to the internal children_suites_ vector, then inserts the suite into the list of suites, sorted by name, deferring execution until run_child_suites() is called. The suite is inserted after it is stored, so that a failed allocation of the vector leaves it out of the list. If tracing is enabled, the suite name is logged for diagnostic purposes.

Once run_suites() has started, the suite is rejected, since it would never run: run_child_suites() takes the number of suites only once, before running them, and after the session has ended nothing runs. The error is reported on stderr, the suite is destroyed when the pointer goes out of scope, and has_rejected_suites_ is set, so that the exit code is not 0; if the session has already ended, the stored exit code is updated, for the later calls of run_suites().

briefdescription.para: Reject a suite constructed after run_suites() has started.

detaileddescription.para: Reports the error on stderr, sets has_rejected_suites_, and, if the session has already ended, updates the stored exit code, for the later calls of run_suites(). Used by register_suite() and by link_static_suite().

name
The name of the rejected suite.
Returns
Nothing.
The message is written on stderr, since the reporter may have ended. The suite itself is destroyed by the caller.

briefdescription.para: Runs all registered test suites.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the suites registered with add_suite() and the static suites that refer to this runner in a single order, sorted by name; for equal names, in the order of their insertion into the list, so the static suites constructed before main() run first. The suites not selected by the first filter pattern are reported as skipped.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Runs the suites registered with add_suite() and the static suites that refer to this runner in a single order, sorted by name.

Both kinds of suites are in the list of suites, which suite::link() keeps sorted by name, so no sorting is needed here; the suites of other runners are skipped. The names are compared with std::strcmp(), so in byte order, case-sensitively, and without comparing the numbers by value; the suites with the same name run in the order of their insertion into the list.

Each suite is assigned a 1-based index, following the top suite, if added, in the order of execution. If the first filter pattern selects it, it is executed via suite::run(), and its totals are accumulated into the runner totals; otherwise, it is reported as skipped and counted in skipped_suites_count_, keeping its index, so that the TAP plan remains complete; while the test cases are listed, the skipped suites are not reported. The executed test cases counter is not incremented; suites are not counted as test cases.
The next suite is read after the current one has run, since the suites of the local runners created by the current suite are inserted into the list, and removed again, while it runs.

briefdescription.para: Insert a static suite into the list of suites, or reject it.

detaileddescription.para: Called by the static_suite constructors. A static suite may be constructed before its runner, which must not be accessed then; therefore the runners that have started are kept in a constant-initialised list, which is searched by address. If the runner is in the list, run_suites() has started and the suite would never run, so it is rejected, as by add_suite(); otherwise, it is linked.

test_runner
The runner of the suite.
suite
The suite being constructed.
Returns
Nothing.
Searches the list of the started runners for test_runner, without accessing it, since it may not be constructed yet. If found, the runner reports the rejection; otherwise, the suite is linked. No memory is allocated.

briefdescription.para: The test runner for the µTest++ framework.

detaileddescription.para: The runner class is responsible for managing the registration and execution of test suites within the µTest++ framework. It owns the optional top suite, returned by add_top_suite(), whose test cases run immediately, in main(), and a collection of test suites added with add_suite(), which are run later, by run_suites(). These suites and the static_suite objects that refer to the runner are kept in a single list, sorted by name, independent of the runner object, so the static suites may be constructed before it. run_suites() runs the suites added with add_suite() and the static suites together, in a single order, sorted by name; for equal names, in the order of their creation, so the static suites constructed before main() run first. The names are compared byte by byte, as by std::strcmp(), not in the order of addition: the comparison is case-sensitive ("Zeta" before "alpha") and does not compare numbers by value ("Suite 10" before "Suite 2"); zero-padded numeric prefixes ("01 - Init") give an explicit order.

Several runners may coexist, global or local, each with its own static suites and suites added with add_suite(). The list of suites is shared by all the runners; each suite refers to its runner, and run_suites() runs only the suites that refer to this runner, skipping those of the other runners, so the runners do not interfere. The list is not protected by a lock: the runners must not run, and the suites must not be created or destroyed, concurrently from different threads.

The test runner provides member functions for initialising the test environment (including the creation of the reporter selected by the runner_options passed to initialise()), registering test suites, and determining the overall test result via an exit code. It also offers an abort mechanism for terminating test execution in exceptional circumstances.
Both initialise() and add_top_suite() are optional:
Without initialise(), the default options are used; without add_top_suite(), there is no top suite, and run_suites() runs only the suites added with add_suite() and the static suites.

The runner is not a node of the test tree: it has no name of its own (the names shown in the reports belong to the suites), and it owns the session totals, which accumulate the totals of all the suites.
All members are defined within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.
